references.text: The Israelites were to take wealth with them when they left Egypt, just as the freed slave was to receive gifts from his master.
The Israelites received silver, gold, and clothing from the Egyptians when they were freed from slavery, which parallels the gifts that were to be given to the freed slave.
The blessing of the Lord as a reason for giving generously is a recurring theme in this chapter.
The Lord promises to bless all the work of anyone who treats their slave fairly and generously.
The gift should be given in proportion to the blessing the Lord has given; the same principle applies to offerings during the festivals.
Each person should give according to their ability, in proportion to the blessing the Lord has given, following the same principle as in the release of slaves.
Proverbs encourages honoring the Lord with the firstfruits of all harvests, reflecting generosity from what one has gathered.
